current_evidence: The workbook PDF (official South Tyneside media library, filename 'update 2026 - Final Version', upload timestamp 27 Oct 2026) could not be fetched, while the only dated pages found still show the 2024 list: South Tyneside article 3633 'Validation of Planning Applications in Tyneside 2024 - Published: September 2024', and Newcastle's joint page hosting 'Tyneside Validation Checklist Jan 25 - Final' ('This latest document supersedes the validation checklist published in 2019'). So the 2026 update is probably the newest file, but no page found confirms it was adopted or when.

issues.detail: The List date 2026-10-01 comes from PDF metadata, not from the document text. No council page found gives a 2026 adoption or publication date. South Tyneside's own validation page still describes the list as the 2024 version, published September 2024. The date and the 2026 file's adopted status are unconfirmed.
issues.evidence: southtyneside.gov.uk/article/3633: 'Validation of Planning Applications in Tyneside 2024 ... Published: September 2024'; Date basis = 'PDF metadata CreationDate'

issues.detail: Grokbot built its items from four documents. These are the superseded February 2019 Tyneside list, the 2026 update PDF, the January 2025 PDF hosted by Newcastle, and Newcastle's 'Draft Tyneside Validation Checklist 2024' consultation page. Some app-type rows rely only on the superseded 2019 list: Block plan/Site plan, Cycle parking, Ecological Survey, Heritage Statement (Full planning), Travel Plan (Full) and Minerals/Waste (Householder). Others rely only on the draft consultation page: Design Code/Masterplan, Landscaping (Full) and Marketing (prior approval). Seven tab_items also cite the 2019 PDF.
issues.evidence: Newcastle validation page: 'This latest document supersedes the validation checklist published in 2019'; sources ending Validation_of_Planning_Applications__in_Tyneside_Feb._2019_3.pdf and .../have-your-say-planning/draft-tyneside

issues.detail: About 25 of the 41 tab_items are boilerplate or fragments, not requirements. The data-protection sentence about redacting signatures appears 8 times, with page-number fragments attached ('23 15.', '16.', '60 Checklist 2:', '62 Checklist 3:', '98 Checklist 2:'). Other items are: policy-background lists (Open Space Assessment 2025 / Playing Pitch Mitigation, 'Newcastle and Gateshead Core Strategy Policies CS1, CS13...', 'NPPF – Viability Guidance'); the Newcastle draft consultation page header and contents list ('Click here to view the pdf document ... your chance to comment Contents'); the paper-copies note; and a broken Environment Agency link fragment ('445.pdf Guidance on the assessment of impact to WFD'). The Natura 2000 definition sentences in the policy section ('Special Protection Area (SPA) / Ramsar Site, Special Area of Conservation (SAC);', 'The Directive specifically relates to...') are also fragments.
issues.evidence: tab_items section 'Submission rules' (24 items) and 'Policy-driven requirements' items 1-3

issues.detail: The same drawing-standard and HRA text appears several times, copied from different versions. There are 3 copies of 'Site Plan (Existing and Proposed)...', 2 of the location plan scale (1:1250 or 1:2500), 2 identical 'annotations, north point, scale and key/legend...' items, 2 furniture-layout/space-standards items and 3 copies of the HRA trigger.

Some rows are filed under the very application types the source excludes. 'Coal Mining / Land Stability Risk Assessment' and 'Minerals / Waste specific statements' are listed under Householder, but the quoted text says householder extensions are exempt. The Minerals row is also really the coal-mining text. Under 'Change of use - prior approval', the Block plan/Site plan, Design Code/Masterplan and Landscaping rows rest on text that says '(i.e. excluding applications for change of use only...)' or 'other than wholly change of use/conversion applications'. Marketing Information applies to change-of-use planning applications and to demolition of listed or conservation-area buildings, not to prior approvals.
issues.evidence: Source: Coal Mining Risk Assessment 'with the exception of householder extensions or alterations, changes of use and shop front alterations'

issues.detail: About 50 requirements were placed under Full planning with the note 'INFERRED: application type not named', for example Air Quality, Archaeology, FRA, Affordable Housing, HIA, Contaminated Land and Viability. Outline has only Travel Plan and Reserved matters has none, although the list's thresholds apply to outline and reserved matters too (Sustainability Statement says 'major full planning applications and major reserved matter applications'). Listed building consent has only Heritage Statement, but Structural Survey and building recording also apply to listed or locally listed buildings. Demolition in conservation area is '(none)', but Heritage Statement, Structural Survey, Marketing Information and building recording all cover demolition in conservation areas. Advertisement consent is '(none)', although South Tyneside publishes a separate 'Tyneside Validation - Advert Checklist' (article 13046), and the advert illumination row was put under Full planning instead.
issues.evidence: app_type_rows notes 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning'; Newcastle-hosted list: Heritage Statement / Structural Survey / Marketing triggers include demolition in conservation areas

issues.detail: Some app-type rows are not local requirements for South Tyneside. In 'Employment / Economic Statement' the quoted text says it 'would not be required for validation purposes'. 'Pre-application advice / engagement details' is the document's contents list. 'CIL Additional Information / Form' applies only to Newcastle, North Tyneside and Gateshead, since South Tyneside is not a CIL charging authority.
issues.evidence: 'CIL liable development in Newcastle, North Tyneside and Gateshead will be required to provide further information'; requirement 39 'Community Infrastructure Levy (Gateshead, North Tyneside and Newcastle only)'

issues.detail: Many trigger excerpts are cut off, give no trigger, or belong to another requirement. Daylight/Sunlight, Lighting and Tall buildings all read 'When is this required? 72', where 72 is a page number. Archaeology reads 'When is this required? Archaeological desk based assessment', but the real triggers are works near Scheduled Monuments, the Hadrian's Wall corridor, greenfield sites of 1 ha or more, and so on. Minerals reads 'sterilisation of mineral resources.' Marketing reads 'conservation areas Marketing information will not always be required.' Design and Access Statement reads 'Design and Access Statement (if required) 8.' Block plan quotes the national checklist list. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' and 'Construction (Environmental) Management Plan' both quote the SuDS Construction Method Statement text. The advert illumination row ends in data-protection boilerplate. Affordable Housing gives no thresholds, but South Tyneside's are 11+ units in urban fringe villages, 15+ elsewhere, or sites of 0.5 ha or more. The Fire Statement trigger does not say it applies to relevant high-rise residential buildings.
issues.evidence: Tyneside list req. 12: 'South Tyneside: 11+ units in the urban fringe villages ..., 15+ units elsewhere, or housing on sites of 0.5 ha or more'; req. 14 archaeology triggers

issues.detail: Grokbot missed some local requirements. (1) Overheating Assessment and Mitigation (req. 26) applies to residential dwellings, residential institutions, student accommodation and accommodation for children aged 5+ where overheating is a potential significant issue. (2) Historic building recording (part of req. 14) applies to demolition or substantial alteration of 19th-century or older, listed, locally listed or conservation-area buildings. (3) Archaeological field evaluation applies to new building work affecting those areas or sites on the Historic Environment Record. (4) Surface Water Drainage Strategy is required for all major development, but Grokbot's drainage trigger omits this. (5) The vibration survey for development next to rail or Metro lines, and the acoustic trigger for air source heat pumps, are also missing.

summary: Grokbot's link is a South Tyneside 'update 2026' file that could not be fetched, and its date comes from PDF metadata; the council page still shows the 2024 list (published September 2024), so whether the link is current is unconfirmed. The extraction mixes the superseded 2019 list and a draft consultation page with the 2024 and 2026 lists, about 25 of its 41 tab items are boilerplate, and several rows are filed under application types the source excludes or have missing or garbled triggers.

withdrawn_issues.detail: Grokbot's Health Impact Assessment trigger for South Tyneside is '100 or more dwellings and non-residential developments over 1 hectare'. The 2024/Jan 2025 joint list gives major residential over 100 units and employment sites of 10 ha or more. The 2026 PDF could not be fetched, so it is unclear whether the threshold changed or the excerpt is wrong.
withdrawn_issues.evidence: Newcastle-hosted Tyneside list, Health Impact Assessment section
withdrawn_issues.grok_comment: The Tyneside Validation Checklist 2024 gives a separate South Tyneside threshold: "In South Tyneside, a Health Impact Assessment (HIA) is required for residential schemes for 100 or more dwellings and non-residential developments over 1 hectare in size." That matches Grokbot exactly; the 100-unit / 10 ha figures quoted by the audit are the Newcastle and North Tyneside wording.
withdrawn_issues.claude_response: Accepted. The South Tyneside-specific threshold in the 2024 checklist matches Grokbot.
